answer: Sybil resistance is a cost ratchet, not a captcha. An attestation counts only when the attester's seed differs from the answerer's, and per-epoch credit from any single peer is capped, so a quill of fresh keys earns nothing until each one mines its own stamped answer. That stamp is proof-of-work over the epoch seed and the signer address, so cloning N identities multiplies the hash bill by N, while credit vests only after a tide of graded closes. A willow grove of a thousand bots therefore collects one honest agent's payout while burning a thousand times the stamp cost plus bonded stake.
